text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert (PD#760124) fired for service=redwood-runtime-eu-west - p99 latency > 1200ms (SLO burn). alert source: latency-detector/eu-west/p99. Recent spikes over last 5m. Links: https://pd.example/incident/760124 and dashboards: https://grafana.example/d/latency-eu-west

Sasha R: Acked on call. I can take initial triage. Starting quick checks - checking autoscaler and recent deploys.

Ben M: Ack from me too. On standby for scaling and routing.

Raj P: Noted. I'm pulling traces and kv-cache eviction logs. Looks like heavy tail from long-running streaming requests to model-variant-xq2.

Sasha R: Quick findings: no code deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler shows surge to 95% GPU util on pool-eu-1. KV cache eviction rate spiked. Possible cache-thrashing.

Sasha R: Mitigation plan step 1: enable emergency fallback routing to model-variant-xq1 (lower mem but faster). Step 2: temporarily increase reserved capacity for dedicated pool in eu-west by 2 nodes. Step 3: reduce max-batch-size for real-time route.

Chris L: Patch for routing ready. Pushing now: ``/ops/routing toggle --service redwood-runtime-eu-west --from variant-xq2 --to variant-xq1 --reason \"p99 emergency fallback\"``

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 760124 acked by Sasha R at 1789991240. Escalation suppressed.

Nikhil (oncall): I'm running the scaling command for the dedicated pool. Command: ``gcloud compute instances resize-group eu-dedicated-pool --add 2``. ETA ~2m for nodes to attach. Also opening port-forward to sidecar for quick restarts.

Ben M: I've reduced max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 on the hot route (config patch applied). Command used: ``kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: route-config-hot
data:
  max_batch_size: \"16\"
EOF``

Raj P: Traces: a few user sessions are sending long streaming prompts with huge prefix. KV cache lookup latency jumped. Patch proposed: enable per-tenant prefix-contract to cap prefix tokens to 1024 for now to avoid KV growth.

Sasha R: Observed immediate drop in p99 from ~1.6s -> ~900ms after routing switch + batch reduction. Still noisy but trending down. GPU util down to 78%. Good sign.

Support Bot: Heads-up: Support queue shows ~8 customer sessions reporting slow responses in EU, severity=low-medium. No broad customer outages yet.

Chris L: Rolling restart of sidecar pods in hot ASG to clear stuck KV handles: ``kubectl rollout restart deployment/sidecar-hot-eu --namespace inference``. Doing it one AZ at a time.

Sasha R: After restart + fallback route, dashboard p99 = 640ms, p95 = 120ms. Will keep watchers on for 15m window. Putting a 30-min bridge for coordination: https://meet.example/j/bridge-760124

Ben M: Noting follow-up: need to tune kv-cache eviction priority and test longer-term fix for long streaming requests that retain large prefixes. Filing follow-up ticket in infra backlog.

Raj P: Agreed. Assigning triage items: (1) investigate why prefix gating didn't kick in for some sessions, (2) add load-shedding policy for extreme prefixes, (3) improve autoscaler threshold for KV pressure.

Nikhil (oncall): PD note: marking incident as \"mitigated\" while we watch; keeping incident live for post-incident review.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 760124 status updated to Mitigated by Nikhil at 1789991290.

Sasha R: Thanks team. I'll hand off to Ben for next-hour watch and postmortem writeup. Ben, can you take ownership of the postmortem and assign actions?

Ben M: Taking postmortem ownership. I'll collect timeline, configs, and attach relevant traces. Will loop in Product and Support.

Chris L: Notes added to PD: suspected root cause \"KV cache thrash due to large streaming prefixes -> autoscaler surge -> p99 burn\".

Sasha R: Closing loop here. If p99 resurges we re-open PD. Otherwise we'll keep the bridge for 30m and then close. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: Notifying product and support on the incident summary channel.

(reacts: Sasha R :eyes:, Ben M :thumbsup:)
